English.overview: Disease Identification: Diagnosed with Apple - Apple scab (Confidence Score: 90.0%). Pathology & Impact: This phytopathogenic infection affects foliage, producing necrotic spots, chlorotic yellow halos, and premature leaf drop. Under high humidity, unmanaged infection can lead to 30% to 60% potential yield reduction.
English.chemical: Recommended Chemical Control Plan: • Foliar Fungicide Spray: Apply Copper Oxychloride 50% WP at 2.5g per Liter of water (approx. 500g per acre). • Systemic Fungicide (Severe Spread): Rotate with Mancozeb 75% WP (2g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (1ml/L). • Application Window: Spray early morning or late evening. Re-apply after 10 to 12 days if heavy rain occurs.
English.biological: Organic & Biological Remedies: • Neem Oil Spray: Mix Neem Oil (10,000 PPM) at 5ml/Liter with 1ml liquid emulsifier. • Biocontrol Agent: Apply foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens or Trichoderma viride (5g/L). • Sanitation: Immediately prune and burn heavily infected leaves.
English.preventative: Preventative & Cultural Best Practices: • Crop Spacing: Maintain proper plant spacing to maximize solar radiation and canopy airflow. • Irrigation: Switch to Drip Irrigation to avoid leaf wetness from overhead watering. • Nutrient Management: Avoid excessive Nitrogen; apply balanced Potassium & Organic Compost.
English.advice: Prune infected leaves immediately, apply Copper Oxychloride or Neem Oil, and manage drip irrigation.
